claims.statement: An account bill is described as its plan plus additional subscriptions and usage charges for that account. This account-specific composition does not establish current prices, actual consumption, invoice amounts or shared billing.

The fragment navigates to Billing and licensing under Access in a settings sidebar, using a decorative credit-card icon. Navigation alone does not confer billing authority or record a visited financial account.

Billing overview navigation differs by account type: organization settings sidebar Access versus enterprise top-level Billing & Licensing tab. Those UI paths are contextual instructions, not authorization or live capability verification.

The pinned quota table gives plan-specific artifact storage/monthly minutes/per-repository cache/custom-image storage: Free personal and Free organizations 500 MB/2000/10 GB/not applicable; Pro 1 GB/3000/10 GB/not applicable; Team 2 GB/3000/10 GB/75 GB; Enterprise Cloud 50 GB/50000/10 GB/150 GB. Units and denominators differ; this historical table does not establish current entitlements, larger-runner inclusion, usage or a spending grant.

The pinned standard-runner table records USD per-minute SKU rates: Linux x64 one-core actions_linux_slim 0.002; Linux x64 two-core actions_linux 0.006; Linux arm64 two-core actions_linux_arm 0.005; Windows x64/arm64 two-core actions_windows/actions_windows_arm 0.010 each; macOS three/four-core M1 or Intel actions_macos 0.062. This is pinned historical pricing evidence, not verified current pricing, budget approval or a calculated workload bill.

After enabling the templated advanced-security code-security or secret-protection product, usage reporting may lag up to two hours in Billing and licensing. The filename mentions Actions but content scope is the security product; reporting lag is not absent usage, no cost or failed activation.

Azure permission acceptance is conditional on reviewing the prompt and agreeing to its terms. The fragment does not establish specific permission scopes, consent, credentials or authorization to accept on the user's behalf.
The Azure subscription selection step chooses the intended Subscription ID for account connection. Selection guidance is not an authorized connection, confirmed identity or billing change.

The fragment points to the general billing getting-started parent for payment methods and payment history. The outbound reference is not inherited review of that article, an actual payment record or permission to open financial settings.
The isolated Create budget click is a contextual UI step. It does not define amount, scope, stopping behavior or alerts and cannot establish an approved budget or authorize its creation.
